description: On startup, seeds the working rules file from the shipped default unless it already exists. On every session start, and whenever the data-directory rules file changes, narrows agents/ to the fleet agents those rules let anyone reach, watches that file, and asks each session for /reload-plugins when its set changed; an invalid rules or models file leaves agents/ as it is, and a session with FLEET_RULES set leaves agents/ to the data-directory file. At every session start it also adds a summary of the MCP tool lists in the rules file in force, the one FLEET_RULES names included, to the session's context while either list is not empty or the lists are invalid. Before every Agent, Skill, Workflow, Bash and MCP tool (mcp__*) call, identifies the caller (an empty agent_id is the main session, whatever agent_type says; a payload that is not one JSON object with an object tool_input, or whose agent_id, agent_type, tool_name, hook_event_name or transcript_path is neither a string nor null, is refused, except at an MCP call, where a payload whose text does not hold "agent_id" passes before it is parsed): the main session's Agent calls are checked against the main section and its other calls pass, its MCP calls even without jq or a rules file when the payload's text does not hold "agent_id" (one that holds it, in a tool argument say, goes through the usual checks, which need jq and a rules file); a fleet subagent's Agent calls are checked against its row in rules, its Skill and Bash calls against the disallowed lists, its MCP calls against the global allowed_mcp_tools and disallowed_mcp_tools lists together with the allow and deny rules a block at the top of a fleet agent's brief may add, for the caller and for every fleet agent above it, found through the session's transcript files: each of those agents must permit the tool (FLEET_MCP_DENIED); invalid lists, an invalid block, or a brief or ancestry that cannot be read or bound refuse the call with FLEET_MCP_ERROR, and the global lists are never used alone in their place; and its Workflow calls are refused; an Agent call to a fleet agent, from either, is refused unless the rules file mentions its model, and must pass one of the levels the rules give that model (any named level when they give none, no effort when they give only default; default beside named levels, or an effort entry other than low, medium, high, xhigh, max and default, is a configuration error that refuses the call), and a missing, relative or unknown effort is refused; the fleet is the set of models the rules file mentions, one agent type per model, recognised by its definition or, when that file is gone, by its model id in the rules, and a type carrying the fleet prefix that neither resolves is refused; a type with another plugin's prefix is not a fleet agent, and a type whose prefix cannot be compared is refused; built-in subagents pass, but only once the rules have been read. The guard passes a call only on its own explicit decision: a call whose check does not finish within 3 seconds, or whose guard stops on an error or on a signal it can trap, is refused, but a kill the guard cannot trap ends it without a decision and is not refused; the 3-second limit covers the check, not the short steps of the process that supervises it. A rules file that is not exactly one JSON object (an empty file, several documents, a top-level array or string, text that is not JSON; null reads as empty rules) makes these checks refuse. When a fleet agent starts, the same guard hands it the disallowed skills and commands, so it does not try them (a refused skill is not a reason to stop), and, while either global MCP list is not empty or the lists are invalid, a summary of the MCP tool rules in force: the global lists, the rule forms and the per-spawn block; the session start adds the same summary to the session's context. Separately, an Agent call that targets a fleet agent is refused unless its prompt is a structured brief with the required sections, and a block of MCP rules at its top follows the block grammar (at most 256 rules of at most 256 bytes in each list); an Agent call to another agent type, or with no type, is refused when its prompt is a string that opens with such a block, valid or not, which works only for fleet agents, or when reading a string prompt or the block at its top fails; a missing or non-string prompt passes untouched, and nothing else of that prompt is checked.
